dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. How can I help you this afternoon?
Hello, Kevin. Yes, good afternoon. My name is Paula Amaral. I am calling because the water on my street, it is very bad, and I am a little bit nervous about it.
Okay, Paula, sorry to hear that. Where are you, what's the street?
It is 431 Chapel Street, in the Historic Hill. Right by the corner, where the drain is, at the side of the road.
Got it, 431 Chapel. And what's going on there, is it backed up, is it standing water?

Yes, standing, and it is coming up over the curb. The water goes across the whole sidewalk, so you cannot walk there, you must go in the street. And this morning a delivery truck, a big one, it went in the water and it got stuck. They were there a long time.
Oh boy. Stuck like, the wheels in the water, or it stalled out?
I think it stalled, the water was high on the wheels. The man was calling somebody on the phone, and then another truck came to pull it. Now it is gone, but the water is still here.
Okay. And this is from the rain Friday and Saturday?
Yes, the rain Friday and Saturday, two days ago. It stopped Saturday and I thought, okay, tomorrow it goes down. But no. Today it is the same, almost.
So it's not draining at all. Let me write this down. Chapel Street, 431, storm drain at the corner, water over the curb and across the sidewalk, vehicle stalled this morning. Did I get that right?
Yes, that is right. And the cars, they are going so slow through it. Everybody is afraid to go fast, so the traffic is a crawl, like a snail. In the morning it was a line of cars.
Yeah, I bet. People hit that and brake, and it backs everybody up. Is it a lot of traffic there, is that a through street for you?

Yes, many people use it. And there is the little store on the corner, you know, the corner store. The same family has it for many, many decades. The grandmother, then the son, now the grandchildren. The customers, they cannot come in easy with this water at the door.
Sure, I know the kind of place you mean. That's a neighborhood spot. Is water getting into the store, or just at the front?
Just at the front, so far. But I am worried, because if it rains again, it will go inside. I am not sure. [pause] And for me, the water, it is not in my house, but it is close to my steps.
Okay, that's good that it's not inside. Let me ask you a couple things. Do you see leaves or trash or anything sitting on top of the drain, like blocking it?
I cannot see the drain, because it is under the water. But before the rain, there were many leaves and little sticks in the street. Maybe it was already full.

That could be it. Debris packs the grate and then it just can't take anything. Alright, I'm going to open this up as a work order so a crew can go look at the drain and clear it if that's the problem.
Yes, thank you. Please. And can you tell me, the work order, when will it be? What is the date they come? I would like to know, so I can tell the store people also.

Right. So I'll get it entered today, Monday. Typically after a storm like this we've got a stack of drain calls, so it's probably a matter of a few days rather than hours. I'd say look for a crew sometime this week, and if it's blocking traffic like you're describing, I'll flag it so it gets looked at toward the front of the line.
A few days. Okay. This week. So not today, but maybe tomorrow, or Wednesday?

Could be tomorrow, could be Wednesday or Thursday. I don't have the crew schedule in front of me, that's with the supervisor. What I can do is put the request in with a note about the truck and the traffic, and give you the work order number so you can follow up.
Yes, the number, please, I will write it. I have a pencil here.

Sure. Give me one second while it generates. [pause] Okay, it's coming up. I'll read it slow. Hang on, it hasn't assigned yet. Let me put it in first. Is the best callback number the one you're calling from?
Yes, this is my house phone. It is four zero one, five five five, zero one eight seven.
Zero one eight seven, perfect. And it's Paula Amaral, A-M-A-R-A-L?
Yes, correct. Paula, with one L. Amaral, yes.

Great. Okay, it's in. The work order will be dated today, March ninth, for storm drain flooding at 431 Chapel Street. I'll read you the number in a second, I just want to add the note about the stalled truck.
Okay, I wait. No problem.

[pause] Alright, note added: water over the curb and across the sidewalk, delivery truck stalled this morning, traffic slowed to a crawl, corner store entrance affected. That should get somebody's attention.
Thank you, Kevin. That is very good. You are very kind. And the number?

Yeah, so, the system's giving me a reference and I'd rather not have you write down the wrong thing. Let me have the office call you back with it, or you can call this line tomorrow and ask for the request on Chapel Street under your name. Either way it'll be findable.
Okay, I understand. Tomorrow I call and I say Amaral, Chapel Street. Yes?
That's it. Amaral, Chapel Street, storm drain. Anybody here can pull it up.
Good. And if it rains again before they come? Then what do I do? I am scared the water goes in the store, and maybe the cars, they can have damage.

If it gets worse, like water heading toward a building or a car really stuck in a dangerous spot, call us right back and tell us it's escalated. If it's an emergency, someone in danger, you'd call 911. For just the standing water, calling us is right.
Okay. I will do like that. Thank you for the patience, I know I talk a lot, my English, sometimes I go around the bush.
No, you're totally fine, you explained it well. Anything else I can do for you today?
No, that is everything. Only I hope they come soon. Thank you, Kevin. Have a good afternoon.
You too, Paula. Take care, and we'll get somebody out there.
Thank you. Goodbye.
